accepted.question_text: Consider the Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval (0<x<L): u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 for t>0, with initial data u(x,0)=phi(x), and boundary data imposed through one of the four operator families B_k u=~h. In the notation used in the paper these families are built from B_1=(u(0,t),u(L,t),u_x(L,t)), B_2=(u(0,t),u_x(L,t),u_{xx}(L,t)), B_3=(u_{xx}(0,t),u(L,t),u_x(L,t)), and B_4=(u_{xx}(0,t),u_x(L,t),u_{xx}(L,t)), together with the lower-order boundary terms explicitly listed for B_{k,1} in the review. Is this problem globally well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some s>=0? Equivalently, can a solution blow up in finite time in some H^s(0,L) norm, or can one prove the global a priori bound sup_{0<=t<infty}||u(.,t)||_{L^2(0,L)}<infty that would yield global well-posedness?
accepted.context_brief: Global well-posedness for general finite-interval KdV IBVP

evidence.quote: While the results reported in this paper gave a significant improvement in the theory of initial boundary value problems of the KdV equation on a finite interval, there are still many questions to be addressed for the following IBVP: (4.18) ut +ux +uxxx +uux = 0, 0 < x < L, t > 0, u(x,0) = φ(x), Bku =~h.
• Is the IBVP (4.18) globally well-posed in the space Hs(0,L) for some s ≥ 0 or equivalently, does any solution of the IBVP (4.18) blow up in the some space Hs(0,L) in finite time?

Consequently, it suffices to establish a global a priori L2(0,L) estimate (4.19) sup 0≤t<∞ ku(·,t)kL2(0,L) < +∞, for solutions of the IBVP (4.18) in order to obtain the global well-posedness of the IBVP (4.18) in the space Hs(0,L) for any s ≥ 0.

Before presenting the main ideas to prove Theorem G, let us introduce the following boundary operators Bk, k = 1,2,3,4 as Bk = Bk,0 +Bk,1 with B1,0v := (v(0,t),v(L,t),vx (L,t)), B2,0v := (v(0,t),vx(L,t),vxx(L,t)), B3,0v := (vxx(0,t),v(L,t),vx (L,t)), B4,0v := (vxx(0,t),vx(L,t),vxx(L,t)) and B1,1v := (0, 0, 0), B2,1v := (0, b30v(L,t), a21vx(0,t) +b20v(L,t)), B3,1v := (a10v(0,t) +a11vx(0,t), 0, a30v(0,t)).
B4,1v := ( sum j=0 to 1 a1j ∂jx v(0,t) +b10v(L,t), a30v(0,t) +b30v(L,t), sum j=0 to 1 a2j ∂jx v(0,t) +b20v(L,t) ).

accepted.question_text: For the same finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries problem u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 on 0<x<L, t>0, with initial data u(x,0)=phi(x) and boundary condition B_k u=~h taken from the four operator families B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4 described above, is the initial-boundary value problem well-posed in the negative-regularity regime H^s(0,L) for some s<=-1? The review notes that the known local theory reaches s>=0, can be extended to -1<s<=0, and conjectures that the bounded-interval problem is ill-posed for every s<-1.

evidence.quote: While the results reported in this paper gave a significant improvement in the theory of initial boundary value problems of the KdV equation on a finite interval, there are still many questions to be addressed for the following IBVP: (4.18) ut +ux +uxxx +uux = 0, 0 < x < L, t > 0, u(x,0) = φ(x), Bku =~h.
• Is the IBVP well-posed in the space Hs(0,L) for some s ≤ −1?
Theorem G ensures that the IBVP (4.18) is locally well-posed in the space Hs(0,L) for any s ≥ 0. Theorem G can also be extended to the case of −1 < s ≤ 0 using the same approach developed in [8].
We conjecture that the IBVP (4.18) is ill-posed in the space Hs(0,L) for any s < −1.

Before presenting the main ideas to prove Theorem G, let us introduce the following boundary operators Bk, k = 1,2,3,4 as Bk = Bk,0 +Bk,1 with B1,0v := (v(0,t),v(L,t),vx (L,t)), B2,0v := (v(0,t),vx(L,t),vxx(L,t)), B3,0v := (vxx(0,t),v(L,t),vx (L,t)), B4,0v := (vxx(0,t),vx(L,t),vxx(L,t)) and B1,1v := (0, 0, 0), B2,1v := (0, b30v(L,t), a21vx(0,t) +b20v(L,t)), B3,1v := (a10v(0,t) +a11vx(0,t), 0, a30v(0,t)).
B4,1v := ( sum j=0 to 1 a1j ∂jx v(0,t) +b10v(L,t), a30v(0,t) +b30v(L,t), sum j=0 to 1 a2j ∂jx v(0,t) +b20v(L,t) ).

accepted.question_text: Consider the nonlinear Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval 0<x<L: u_t+u u_x+u_{xxx}=0, u(x,0)=phi(x), together with the boundary conditions u(0,t)=0, u(L,t)=0, and u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t). Is this nonlinear problem well-posed in H^s(0,L) for any Sobolev index s?

evidence.quote: Finally, still concerning with well-posedness problem, while the approach developed recently in [18] studies the nonhomogeneous boundary value problems of the KdV equation on (0,L) with quite general boundary conditions, there are still some boundary value problems of the KdV equation that the approach do not work, for example (4.23) ut +uux +uxxx = 0, x ∈ (0,L), u(x,0) = φ(x), u(0,t) = 0, u(L,t) = 0, ux(0,t) = ux(L,t).

As for the IBVP (4.23), its associated linear problem ... has been shown by Cerpa (see, for instance, [20]) to be well-posed in the space Hs(0,L) forward and backward in time. However, the following problem is still unknown: • Is the nonlinear IBVP (4.23) well-posed in the space Hs(0,L) for some s ?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Is the IBVP (4.18), with general boundary condition, controllable?

evidence.quote: Thus, with respect of the control issue, a natural and interesting open problem arises here: • Is the IBVP (4.18), with general boundary condition, controllable?

It was shown in [52] that the exact controllability of the linearized system holds in L2(0,L) if and only if, L does not belong to the following countable set of critical lengths N := {2π/√3 sqrt(k2 +kl +l2) : k, l ∈ N*}.
They proved that system (4.18) with boundary conditions B1,0v is then null controllable, but not exactly controllable, because of the strong smoothing effect.
